chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when the crescent of the month of Ramadan appeared, would face the Qibla and raise his hands and say: 'O Allah, make it appear for us with security and faith, and safety and Islam, and encompassing health, and abundant provision, and repelling of diseases. O Allah, grant us its fasting and its night prayer, and recitation of the Quran within it. O Allah, deliver it to us and accept it from us, and grant us safety within it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when the crescent of Ramadan appears?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) ritual of facing the Qibla and raising hands upon sighting the Ramadan crescent, emphasizing a holistic supplication for spiritual and physical well-being. It underscores the Shia tradition of linking celestial signs with divine mercy, asking specifically for the preservation of the month and the capacity to fulfill its obligations of fasting, night prayer, and Quranic recitation. This practice reflects the broader Islamic emphasis on gratitude and preparation for the 'month of patience' as a means of attaining God-consciousness.
